references.text: Direct continuation of the same dialogue where the condition for becoming one people is set.
The immediate consequence of the condition: marriage and fellowship as a result of circumcision.
Thematic contrast: The desire to be 'like all others' as either sinful rejection of God (1 Sam) or strategic compromise (Gen).
Theological parallel: Human attempt to use God's covenant sign (circumcision) for political unity versus God's actual covenant.
Ironical contrast: Human use of circumcision for survival versus God's requirement of circumcision as a condition for belonging to the people.
Contrast between true covenant obedience (Abraham's house) and strategic mass circumcision for political advantage.
